label: Figure 4
title: How the author's sixty guesses fared against the evidence
caption: The guide began from a private matrix of 60 trade-offs in eight categories with seven observed failure points, which its author called best guesses. Each became a hypothesis and was adjudicated against the sources read in the seven stage sweeps. Twenty rows are supported, 43 are supported with qualifications, four could not be studied because nothing was found either way, none was contradicted, and all eight categories were reframed into the lifecycle stages the selection and turnover literatures use [1](#cite:1) [178](#cite:178) [152](#cite:152) [119](#cite:119). The leading reference column names the source each category's adjudications lean on most.
how_to_read: Each row is one of the original categories, with the stage it became and how its rows came out. A supported row has a cited study or rule behind it; a partly supported row survives with a qualification stated in the ledger; an unstudied row is one the sweeps could not find evidence for or against, and the levers that carry those practices say so. The full ledger, with every adjudication and its citations, is on the methods page.

explain.text: Four rows closed as unstudied: agency fee levels, customer rejection feedback, single requisition ownership and customer approval cycles. The pack carries the practices without evidence of effect and marks them as such.
A category was reframed when the evidence organised its rows differently, for example retention by the ranked turnover predictors rather than by the employee experience [178](#cite:178).

source: Counts are taken from hypotheses.yaml, the guide's own ledger, as closed at version 1.0 on 2026-10-22; the ref column names the reference each category's adjudications cite most. The matrix itself is not in the pack and is never cited as a source of fact.
